 Saleen Martin USA TODAY Nov. 20, 2026, 1:12 p.m. ET Hear this story Honda is recalling over 16,000 vehicles due to a fuel leak that could lead to stalled engines and crashes, according to a release shared on the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s website .
 According to the car manufacturer, the fuel flange joint assembly may have been made without the proper brazing material, causing the parts to loosen and separate.
 If the fuel flange joint separates, fuel could leak and fuel pressure may decrease, causing loss of acceleration, engine stalling. A separated fuel flange joint could also stop the engine from restarting, leading to a crash or injuries.
 Honda said that as of early November, there have been no warranty claims, nor have there been any reports of injuries or deaths related to the recalled vehicles.
 Here’s what we know about the model included in the recall, what led to the recall and what car owners should do.
 Read more: USA TODAY's recall database What model is included in this Honda recall?
 According to the NHTSA, 16,387 total vehicles are included in this recall for the following model:
 2004-2005 Honda S2000

See affected models Parts supplier switched locations, leading to manufacturing issue
 The issue stems back to parts supplier Sanoh Industrial Co.,Ltd., which is also based in Japan. According to Honda, Sanoh Industrial switched locations where the company did its brazing, or combining the metals for the parts.
 After the move, the company did not properly verify its process or work instructions and 67 replacement parts were manufactured incorrectly, or without brazing material. The non-brazed parts were produced and shipped.
 Honda found out about the issue in December 2025. A customer in Japan had recently replaced the fuel flange joint assembly and reported problems with it.
 Honda began investigating the supplier and in January, Honda began looking for a used vehicle to test and figure out what the issue was. In May, Honda conducted tests on the used vehicle and spent the next five to six months investigating. On Nov. 5, the company issued the safety recall.
 What car owners should do if they have a recalled Honda vehicle
 Honda will contact registered owners of the recalled vehicles so they can take their cars to authorized Honda dealers. The dealers will inspect and replace the fuel flange joint assembly with a new part for free.
 The company will let owners know about the remedy by Jan. 4.
